sessions.title: Speed 4×1200 @ 5:40 — nailed it, VO2 up to 44
sessions.verdict: Hit a self-chosen faster target on the number (5:42 avg), strong cadence, shrugged off a fall. Breakthrough-quality.
sessions.headline: This is what the top-end you keep talking about looks like on the clock. You asked to run it faster than planned and then did exactly that — 5:42 against a 5:40 target, right in the band on all four reps. Cadence hit 167–172 (your easy runs sit ~145), stride opened to ~105 cm, and you drove VO2max to a new high of 44. You even fell in rep 3 and still closed rep 4 at 5:47. Genuinely strong day.
insight: On target, all four: R1 5:35 (cad 167) / R2 5:41 (cad 172) / R3 5:45 (cad 161, the fall) / R4 5:47 (cad 162). A controlled positive split from fatigue, not a fade — you held the band even after going down.
Your in-run feel was spot on: cadence WAS best early (167→172) and settled to 161 late. Reading your own turnover that accurately is a real skill, and 167+ at speed is a big step up from ~145 easy.

Real VO2 stimulus: reps at HR 180 (your new recalculated LTHR) with a 193 max is exactly the intensity that pushes the number UP — hence 43→44 (new high), plus LTHR 182→180 and FTP 326→333 W. The engine is climbing.
Resilience banked: fell and scraped the knee in rep 3, took the hit, and still ran rep 4 on pace. That's the kind of day that builds more than fitness.

sessions.title: Technique Day 1.3k — muggy-air morning
sessions.verdict: Easy technique work but HR ran hot (active 150 avg, 184 max). Environmental, not fitness — confirmed muggy low-pressure + Hebbal PM2.5 morning.
sessions.headline: Technique/drill session where the whole pool — and a swimmer in a neighbouring complex — was out of breath. HR sat high for the low effort, traced to a humid, overcast, low-pressure morning with elevated particulate at a 7:27am open-air rooftop pool. Not a fitness red flag.
insight: Active-work HR 150 avg / 184 max is high for technique swimming (should sit low 130s); rests also stayed up (133 avg, 177 max) instead of dropping fast — the fingerprint of harder-to-move air, not threshold effort.

Environmental cause confirmed (web-checked): overcast 23C / 73% RH (dew point ~18C) low-pressure morning + Hebbal AQI ~140 at 07:27, peak inversion window, open-air 13th-floor pool. Neighbouring-complex swimmer felt identical — rules out pool chloramine, ventilation, and personal fitness.

Not hypoxia: barometric dips shave only ~1-2% off O2 partial pressure; it's the perception of air hunger (humidity + particulate) driving breathing rate and HR up. Bengaluru's ~920m baseline amplifies the dip vs a lowland city.
Protocol: on still, overcast monsoon mornings, check PM2.5 before an open-air swim. If 130+, treat as easy/technique by default and ignore the elevated HR.

sessions.title: Easy / recovery run 4.7k — HR-capped (VO2-safe)
sessions.verdict: Cap honored perfectly (142 avg / 157 max). Stopped at 4.7 of 6k on tired legs — correct call the day after the 16k, not a miss.
sessions.headline: Day-after-16k recovery run, executed exactly as designed. HR never came near the ceiling so the watch generated no VO2max data point — legs, not lungs, were the limiter, and stopping early was the right call.
insight: HR discipline: running blocks 142 avg / max 157, fully under the 150 easy cap and the 160 ceiling. This is the VO2-safe easy run we scheduled — no VO2max data point generated, as intended.

Legs, not lungs, ended it: 18 short walk breaks and stopped at 4.7 of 6k, but max HR only 157 — so the walks were leg fatigue from the 16k, not HR-ceiling driven. Bailing early on tired legs was correct, not a miss.
Running-only cadence 145.5 spm — solid for recovery pace and cleaner than walk-diluted long-run numbers; form held (GCT 330ms, vertical ratio 10.6, 206W).
Pace ~9:10/km (running) is slow, but pace is irrelevant on a capped recovery day — HR and how the legs feel are the only metrics. Muggy Bengaluru evening also taxed it.

sessions.title: Long run 16k — two-block HR-capped (base)
sessions.verdict: Textbook execution: block 1 sat at 151, clean negative split. Target behavior, repeated.
sessions.headline: The two-block structure held almost exactly as drawn. Block 1 sat at 151 avg across 9 km — dead center of target — then a clean negative split into a stronger block 2. Second disciplined HR-capped long run in a row; the Jul 19 Z4 blow-up is firmly in the past.
insight: Block 1 easy base (km3-11, 9k): 7:59/km @ avg HR 151, max 168 — bang on the 150-158 band, cap 160. The bulk of the run held the number the whole way.
Block 2 steady (km12-16, 5k): 7:05/km @ avg HR 166 under the 172 cap. 7:05 at 166 is quicker than the Aug 9 comp pace (7:37 at 171) — base work showing up as pace-at-HR.
Walk-recovery fix worked: ~70 short walks let HR settle to ~150 before running again (vs Aug 16's tag-and-go), so block 1 held instead of sawtoothing. Self-diagnosed and applied.

Flags: a max-195 (Z5) spike late in block 2 — a hill or finish surge, brief but 'steady' means no near-max pops. And ~29 min total walking = easy running pace still drives HR to the ceiling; aerobic base is still the limiter, so watch for walking LESS as the block progresses.

sessions.title: CSS TEST — 400 + 192 TT (+ 3×336 aerobic)
sessions.verdict: First real swim benchmark: CSS = 2:18/100m. Clean, valid test.
sessions.headline: The number this whole exercise was for: CSS = 2:18/100m. Both TTs honest (HR 171–173, redlined to 190 on the 192), full recovery between so they didn't contaminate each other. Breaststroke stayed in the WU/first-336/CD — never the TTs — so the test is clean.
insight: Training paces off CSS: speed ~2:14, threshold (CSS) 2:18, endurance ~2:26 per 100m (per 16 m length: ~21.5 / ~22 / ~23.5 s). Apply S2 @ ~2:26, S3 @ ~2:18, speed reps just under CSS.

11 s/100m spread between the 400 (2:09) and 192 (1:58) = big fatigue slope. Top-end speed is there; fatigue resistance over distance is the developing quality — exactly the profile. As base builds, the 400 pace creeps toward the 192 and CSS drops.

Best qualitative note: 'most unbroken I've swum — rest between sets, not within.' Continuous hold of form and pace IS the aerobic quality we want, worth more than any single fast split. 3×336 done continuous.

3×336 pace vs HR (20s rest): rep2 2:20/100m @ HR 168, rep3 ~2:24 @ HR 158. Pace sat at CSS but effort didn't — rep3 was cleanly aerobic (13–15 bpm under threshold HR), so the set was mixed, not a threshold grind. It felt easy because it was broken, swim HR reads low, and it's his best discipline — in the pool, trust pace + HR over RPE.
Feedback: keep the 3×336 and any aerobic filler freestyle so the pace means something — breaststroke there just makes it easier filler and won't build the freestyle engine.

sessions.title: Swim — endurance + speed (NOT the CSS test)
sessions.verdict: Even-paced main set on a tired body; CSS test still pending
sessions.headline: Endurance + speed swim the morning after the train-sleep run. The two big reps were paced beautifully; efficiency held. This was NOT a valid CSS test — that 400+200 TT is still owed on a rested day.
insight: Highlight: 2×272 m at 2:16.3 and 2:16.8/100m — half a second apart across 272 m each. Same pacing discipline as the run reps, now showing in the pool too.
Efficiency held: SWOLF 31 on both big reps (no decay under distance) — technique held, not just muscled.
Speed set 5×32 m descended then wobbled (1:40→1:47→1:52→2:01→1:45), HR to 178 — mid-set fade is fatigue from the week, not form.

NOT a CSS test: the session was controlled 272 m reps, not the maximal 400+200 TT the plan wants. No valid CSS number produced. Testing max on a depleted body would give a garbage number anyway — do it rested this week.
Load flag: VO2 run at 188 bpm on no sleep + this swim (TE 3.3 aerobic / 2.2 anaerobic) inside ~24 h. System is stacking — keep the Posterior lift light and tomorrow genuinely easy.

sessions.title: Speed 5×1000 @ 5:55 (LT reps)
sessions.verdict: Textbook even pacing — but run on no sleep, HR redlined
sessions.headline: Ran the same session from a few weeks ago on a wrecked battery (slept upright on a train). Pacing was near-perfect; HR blew past threshold because of the sleep debt — not a fitness read.
insight: Pacing was the win: 5:58 / 6:01 / 5:58 / 5:59 / 5:56 — dead-even, no rep-1 surge, no fade. The pacing discipline held.
HR was the story: reps ran 182–189 avg (LTHR 182), maxing 196 — at/above threshold the whole time. Garmin logged it VO2max (TE 4.2), i.e. run harder than the sub-LT cruise it was written as.
Cause: no real sleep (train) + evening heat + AM load. Same pace cost far more cardiovascularly. Effort read is invalid as a fitness signal — discard the bad execution score.

Cadence decayed under fatigue: 158→162→156→154→154, dropping under the 155 floor on the last two reps while pace held — i.e. overstriding crept in (GCT 287 ms). A fatigue signature, not a form regression.
Re-test value pending: when rested, expect this exact session at LOWER HR with cadence held >155. Today's is too compromised to compare fairly.

sessions.title: Long run 17k (HR-capped, aerobic)
sessions.verdict: Longer and lower HR — base trending right
sessions.headline: Ran 2k longer than Aug 9 at a lower average HR — post-illness, in the morning. The aerobic base is trending exactly right.
insight: First morning-start run of the block: no evening-heat HR tax, so this is the cleanest aerobic read yet.
Block 1 easy (km1-12) avg HR 154 at ~7:55/km; Block 2 steady (km13-17) avg HR 163 at ~7:39/km. HR discipline held on both.
17k at avg HR 156 vs the Aug 9 15k at 161: longer AND lower — the aerobic-base signal these runs are built to produce.
Cadence 138 avg (overstriding on easy pace) but climbed to 150+ on the faster kms. Keep nudging easy-pace turnover toward 155+.

sessions.title: Speed repeats (fartlek)
sessions.headline: Ignoring compliance — an encouraging session. Top-end is in better shape than easy-run HR suggests.
insight: First non-zero anaerobic TE (2.8) in ages — the fartlek does what HR-capped long runs structurally can't.
Held 4:40–5:00/km reps at HR only 165–172 (under 182 LTHR) — genuine speed produced sub-threshold. Confirms the limiter is aerobic base, not top-end.
Cadence hit 163–168 on the good reps (vs habitual 143); power 340–410W. Mechanics wake up when you ask for speed.
Overshot nearly every rep — ran 20–40s/km faster than target. 'Not hard physiologically' tricked you into pushing. Load 153 ≈ a 15k long run.
Fix is a skill: aim for the SLOW end of the band. Pacing accuracy > pace. Next quality = 5×1000 @ 5:55 (distance polices the overshoot).

sessions.title: Recovery run (HR-capped)
sessions.headline: The easy-day discipline that's been the hard part — nailed.
insight: Avg HR 134, max 145 — never near the 150–158 cap, one day off a 15k. Exactly the restraint that was missing pre-pivot.
Load 11.7 aids recovery rather than adding fatigue. Pace ~10:40/km is an output here, not a fitness signal.
Cadence 143 — low-stakes on recovery days, but the standing nudge toward 155+ still applies.

sessions.title: Long progression (5+5+5)
sessions.headline: The behaviour change that matters: sub-172 held for the whole run.
insight: Block 3 comp-pace avg never crossed 172 — a complete reversal of the Jul 19 Z4 blow-up.
At the sub-172 ceiling, comp pace was ~7:37/km (not the 7:10 predictor) — sustainable pace anchored to 7:35.
Anaerobic 0.0 is correct by design for an HR-capped sub-threshold run. VO₂max ticked 41→43; status Productive.

swim.css_test: Swim a 400m TT and a 200m TT (full rest between). CSS/100 = (400−200 dist) ÷ (400time − 200time). Sets the threshold pace for quality reps.

strength_split.rule: 2 sets per exercise — except barbell bench, which gets 3 on the Anterior day (the lift driving the 100 kg goal).
strength_split.note: Built lopsided on purpose: swimming (2-3x/wk) already floods back, lats and rear delts, so the gym protects pressing and arms. Bench stays actual barbell on both exposures; keep heavy leg work off long-run and hardest-swim days.
strength_split.volume_note: Back (~8 gym sets + 2-3 swims) is by far the most-trained region. If shoulders feel stacked, the Upper-day pulldown is the first thing to trim.
